| AR-02 | No inventory row owns the Rust crate itself. Every source row names a bare path (W01 src/plan/tree.rs, W10 assets/nav.js, W12 tests/router.rs) that resolves to nothing: the repository has no src/, no assets/, no Cargo.toml (verified by ls at repo root). There is no work unit for Cargo.toml, for the crate root (main.rs or lib.rs) and its module declarations, for the CLI argument surface the binary must expose (the flags overview-serve.sh and the runtime servers pass today: --plan-dir, --out, --refresh, --watch, --serve, plus a --port), or for where the crate lives inside the repository. plan §6.2 leaves this explicitly unresolved ('currently scaffolded as a spike at a path outside the repository, plus wherever the prebuilt artifacts land') while W17 already ships those artifacts and W19 already builds five of them, so two units depend on a location no unit decides. | Add inventory rows owning the crate location, Cargo.toml, the crate root and module tree, and the CLI argument surface with its flag contract; then restate every source row's File as a repository-relative path under that location. | 💤 open | N/A |
| AR-03 | The producer of 'the state document' is unowned, and on the declared Windows target it cannot exist. W02 parses the state document into typed values, while plan §5.2 keeps overview-state.sh as-is ('read for its field contract but its extraction is not redesigned here'). overview-state.sh is a bash script that sources plan-document-lib.sh and calls jq six times (planning/scripts/overview-state.sh:14-17). Nothing in the inventory either ports extraction into Rust or owns the binary invoking that script as a subprocess. §9.4 declares x86_64-pc-windows-msvc a shipped artifact and Windows a target, where neither bash nor jq nor the plan-document library is available, so a Windows host would have a renderer with no state to render. W01 reading the plan tree directly and W02 parsing a separate state document are also two different input paths with no stated relationship. | Decide and record where state comes from: either an inventory row porting overview-state.sh's extraction into the crate (and stating whether the shell script remains for other consumers), or a row owning the subprocess invocation plus an explicit statement that Windows is not supported. Reconcile W01 and W02 so there is one input path. | 💤 open | N/A |
| AR-04 | Nine files that must change have no inventory row, and the two removal units contradict their own atomicity checkbox. Verified by search: planning/templates/plan-overview.html.tmpl (the at-underscore token template §5.3 says goes, deleted by nobody), planning/scripts/overview-serve.sh (the dispatcher; W16 removes only planning/scripts/runtime), planning/requires.tsv (four soft rows in the any-of group overview-server-runtimes whose 'why' text names overview-serve.sh and render-plan-overview.sh; install.sh:377,403,420,432 is generated from them), planning/PACKAGE-MANIFEST.tsv and planning/PACKAGE-MAP.tsv (each lists all eight overview files), planning/SKILL.md:1278 (the documented command line), planning/docs/README.md:18,21, and planning/tests/test-plan-overview.sh, test-overview-serve.sh, test-plan-dir-synonym.sh:100,214 and test-portability-contract.sh:72,86 which hard-code the removed paths. W15's instructions §5.1 say 'Remove ... and every reference to it in the skill, the manifest and the tests' while its atomicity checkbox asserts 'No other file, symbol, test target, or verification flow changes here' - both cannot be true. installer/src/50-manifest.sh:6-9 states its planning list is a deliberate second copy of PACKAGE-MANIFEST.tsv cross-checked by planning/tests/test-installer-manifest.sh, so W17 editing only the manifest source makes that gate red. validate-plan.sh also already warns that 02-step-remove-jq-renderer.md uses an unregistered command literal. | Add inventory rows owning each of those files (template deletion, overview-serve.sh deletion, requires.tsv group removal, both package registries, SKILL.md and docs/README.md, and each affected test), correct W15 and W16 to own only their own file, and register or remove the command literal the validator flags. | 💤 open | W15 |
| AR-05 | Ten test work units are never executed by any gate. W05, W12, W25, W30, W35, W44, W52, W57, W62 and W74 are cargo tests (tests/state_parse.rs, tests/router.rs and so on). run-tests.sh:87 discovers tests with find -maxdepth 1 -type f -name 'test-*.sh' over tests/, planning/tests/ and benchmark/planning/tests/ only, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:48,107 runs ./run-tests.sh. No inventory row adds a cargo leg to run-tests.sh, to ci.yml, or to verify-both-shells.sh, and no row declares the Rust toolchain as a development dependency. W48's instructions enumerate the gates it runs (two-shell harness, installer freshness, mode markers, skill files, probe-versus-declaration, portability catalogue) and cargo test is not among them, so every Rust test could be red and every declared gate still green. | Add an inventory row owning the cargo test leg in run-tests.sh and in ci.yml, a row or constraint declaring the Rust toolchain as a dev dependency with its floor version, and extend W48's acceptance criteria to include the cargo suite. | 💤 open | W48 |
| AR-07 | Seven definition-of-done coverage rows name proofs that do not exist in the dependency graph. validate-plan.sh reports W15, W19, W27, W52, W53, W57 and W67 as graph leaves that nothing depends on. The coverage table nevertheless claims 'W27 and W29 render them ... W31 verifies no clipping' although W31 depends on W30 which depends on W29 and never on W27, and no test unit's instructions mention render_finding, so the finding page has no automated proof at all. The same holds for 'W53 selects the subject, W44 pins it' - W44 depends on W43 and pins active_states, not autoplay_subject - and for W67 (render_transition), W57, W52, W19 (the artifact matrix, which W49 claims to verify while depending only on W48) and W15 (the deletion W48 claims to defend while not depending on it). The coverage table therefore asserts verification relationships the executable order cannot deliver. | Either add the missing dependency edges so each named proof actually follows its subject, or add test units that pin render_finding, autoplay_subject and render_transition and correct the coverage rows to name proofs that exist. | 💤 open | N/A |
| AR-08 | The story table contradicts the plan and the request about autoplay in planning state. US-64 expects 'Autoplay is unavailable and says why, rather than presenting a toggle that cannot follow anything; the same holds for a complete plan' and lists W53 as a related unit. W53 says the opposite: 'Autoplay exists in every mode; the mode decides what it follows ... In planning mode it follows the plan being built: units appearing, dependency edges forming'. US-67 assumes the W53 behaviour ('With the page served on a plan in planning state and autoplay on, add a work unit'). The user's request asks specifically for planning-state autoplay as a node-and-edge animation, so US-64 encodes the rejected behaviour as an acceptance criterion and two stories now cannot both pass. plan §8.6 also still lists complete-mode autoplay as an unresolved open question while US-63 and US-64 already answer it. | Rewrite US-64 to match W53 (autoplay available in planning mode, following plan construction) or delete it, and close §8.6 with a recorded decision for complete mode before W53 is executed. | 💤 open | W53 |
| AR-06 | Shipping prebuilt binaries breaks two existing gates that no unit owns. tests/test-mode-markers.sh:66-80 requires every file listed by skill_files() to carry a '# MODE:' or HTML-comment marker in its first 25 lines; its exempt() list covers only fixtures, .json and .jsonl and .pub, the three planning/scripts/runtime interpreter payloads, the two package registries and .gitignore. A compiled binary cannot carry a marker at all, and there is no arm for it, for assets CSS (W64, W65, W66) or for asset JavaScript outside planning/scripts/runtime (W10, W11, W42, W43, W55, W56, W61, W68, W72, W73), so W17 turns that gate red. Separately, skill_files() (installer/src/50-manifest.sh:39-70) is a flat hand-written heredoc with no platform conditional and 50-manifest.sh:6-9 forbids restructuring it, so all five artifacts would ship to every host; package.json 'files' includes planning wholesale, so they also land in the npm tarball. Nothing owns per-platform selection at install time - W18 only prints a notice. | Add inventory rows owning the mode-marker exemption arms for binaries, CSS and asset JS, and owning per-platform artifact selection in the installer plus the npm packaging consequence; state the committed artifact size the repository and the published package will carry. | 💤 open | W17 |
| AR-09 | plan §8.2 records a mechanism I can show is false. It hypothesises that runtime/overview-server.py 'invokes render-plan-overview.sh with a --serve flag, the plan directory, and an --out path, so if --out is not a supported flag the render fails'. Both flags are supported and documented: render-plan-overview.sh:39 '--out FILE write to FILE instead of plan/overview.html', :42 '--serve', and the parser arms at :55 and :57. I ran the exact command overview-server.py:66 builds against the 173 KB navigation fixture: exit 0, a 181,335-byte page. §2.2 of the same plan already states 'The same renderer invoked directly exits 0', which contradicts the §8.2 hypothesis outright. The plan then defers the defect to 'its own bug entry' - no such entry exists in BUGS.json (B47 and B48 are the socat rung and its CI gap, both fixed). Because the false mechanism is the plan's reason for putting the defect out of scope, the scope boundary rests on a refuted claim; note the load-bearing §2.1 claim itself does reproduce exactly (state 341,088 bytes, render exit 126, 'planning/scripts/render-plan-overview.sh: line 436: /usr/bin/jq: Argument list too long'). | Replace the §8.2 hypothesis with a measured cause or mark it explicitly untested with no mechanism asserted, and file the bug entry the paragraph promises before relying on it to bound scope. | 💤 open | N/A |

None of these states exists in either declared fixture and no inventory row builds them. The two declared fixtures are also user data that cleanup-plans.sh and remove-plan.sh can change or delete, so evidence recorded against them is not reproducible. | Add inventory rows owning a checked-in fixture set that carries each required edge case, or record for each such story the fixture it runs against and who creates it; state whether the two live plans are copied into repository fixtures before being used as evidence. | 💤 open | N/A |
| AR-11 | The user's explicit memory requirement has no verification anywhere. The request states the rewrite is needed because large plans hit limits and asks to keep memory in mind, avoiding per-substitution temporary strings. W07 asserts the property ('One preallocated output buffer, values written as slices, no per-key rebuild') but no test or verification unit measures allocation, peak resident memory, or the absence of per-substitution temporaries. W06 and W47 record only state size and wall time; W69 records frame times in the browser. So the plan can be executed with a renderer that allocates a fresh string per field and every declared gate still passes, which is the defect class the plan exists to remove. | Add a verification unit that records peak memory and allocation behaviour for the 337 KB fixture with a stated ceiling, and name the mutation that fails it (for example replacing the single output buffer with per-field string concatenation). | 💤 open | W07 |
| AR-12 | Two constraint paragraphs still assert the decision the plan reversed. plan §7.1 says 'A compiled binary is therefore optional and additive; no install may be blocked by a missing artifact, and the jq path must keep working' and §7.4 says 'The user has decided: optional binary with bash fallback'. §4.3, §5.3 and §10.4 say the opposite, W15 deletes render-plan-overview.sh outright, and the user's instruction was to scrap the jq fallback entirely. §10.4 records the reversal but leaves §7.1 and §7.4 uncorrected, so the plan states both decisions and an executor reading Constraints and decisions as binding would keep the jq renderer and treat W15 as out of contract. | Rewrite §7.1 and §7.4 to state the current decision - the binary is the only renderer, and a platform with no artifact has no overview - or move the superseded wording into the discards section explicitly labelled as what an earlier version said. | 💤 open | W15 |
| AR-13 | Every crate path in the plan contradicts the repository's codified layout and about fifty of them are ambiguous. CODE-STYLE.md section 1b states that a shipped binary gets one directory per binary under src/, holding that crate's own Cargo.toml, rust-toolchain.toml and src/*.rs, and that a binary does not live inside the skill that uses it. W77 places the crate manifest at planning/overview/Cargo.toml, inside the skill, and every Rust unit names a path relative to an implied crate root: src/plan/tree.rs, src/render/shell.rs, src/pages/graph.rs, tests/router.rs, tests/state_parse.rs, assets/graph.js and so on, about fifty rows. Read as repository paths, which is how every other inventory row in this plan reads, tests/router.rs lands in the repository's own tests/ directory, the one run-tests.sh discovers test-*.sh in, and src/ is the directory section 1b reserves for one subdirectory per binary. The plan therefore names no single location that is both correct and unambiguous, and an executor following it literally would create a second crate root at the repository root. Section 1b also requires crate sources to carry MODE: DEV and PACKAGE: PROD on the first two lines; no unit owns those markers on the roughly forty Rust files the plan creates. | Re-root the crate at src/plan-overview and rewrite every crate-relative inventory row and step change-target under it, so each path reads from the repository root exactly as every non-crate row does. Add a unit owning the MODE and PACKAGE markers on the crate sources, or record where section 1b's requirement is discharged. | 💤 open | N/A |
